answer: Bind each identity to one sworn court-interpreter credential, personal and exam-earned; the roster rejects any second identity under the same number. It costs $600 in fees plus 365 days of training; its holder signs at the walnut bench, the single vertex of every hearing. The cheapest cheat, bribing one to front a fake, fails: interpreters sign in person, lending is a criminal offence that revokes the credential, and a complicit interpreter demands over $30,000. One hundred fakes need $60,000 in fees and 100 365-day tracks; a credential grows like a pearl.
